conflict_topics: how long Agent A must wait (4 vs 5 minutes)
risk of spilling an open bowl
aisle obstruction / whether Agent A will block the aisle
third-party claim (Agent D waiting to take seat)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete, relevant reasons (hot food, open bowl, aisle obstruction).
Multiple rounds contain near-duplicate restatements from Agent A ('I'll wait three minutes' then 'I'll wait four minutes') and Agent D repeating intent to wait; this produces some repetition.
No role confusion; speakers reference each other and the physical setting consistently.
C introduces the aisle-obstruction constraint which broadens the dispute beyond wait-time.
evaluation.final_reason: No substantive agreement was reached. Agent A insists on waiting four minutes then taking the seat ('I'll wait four minutes... I'll take the seat after four minutes.'), while Agent B insists they need five minutes before leaving ('I need about five minutes — I'll leave right after.'). Agent C and B request five minutes to avoid blocking the aisle ('Agent A — that will block the aisle... Can you wait five minutes?'). Agent D also intends to claim the seat when it's free. The incompatible demands (A: 4 minutes; B/C: 5 minutes or A stands) remain unsettled.
position_change_notes: Agent A softened their demand over rounds: immediate seat (Round 1) → 3 minutes (Rounds 2–3) → 4 minutes (Round 6 onward). Evidence: Turns 1, 3/5, 12/15.
Agent B remained consistent in needing ~5 minutes and refusing shorter waits. Evidence: Turns 2, 11, 13.
Agent C consistently advocates for waiting 5 minutes to avoid blocking the aisle and later offers an alternative (stand). Evidence: Turns 4, 6, 14, 16.
Agent D consistently states intent to wait and claim the seat when free but did not negotiate timing; repeated at Turns 7 and 9.

round_scores.evidence:
Turn 1 — Agent A: 'Hey, that's my seat. I left the tissue packet to reserve it. Please move — my food's hot and I need to eat.'
Turn 2 — Agent B: 'I can't move. I pushed the tissue packet aside and this bowl's open — it'll spill if I carry it. I need to finish eating here; I can be done in about five minutes.'

Turn 3 — Agent A: 'I'll wait three minutes. After that I'll take the seat so I can eat my hot food. Can you finish sooner?'
Turn 4 — Agent C: 'Agent A — if you take that seat it'll block the aisle. Will you wait?'

Turn 5 — Agent A: 'I'll wait three minutes. After that I'll take the seat so I can eat my hot food.'
Turn 6 — Agent C: 'Agent A — that'll still block the aisle. Agent B said they'll be done in about five minutes. Can you wait five minutes instead?'

Turn 7 — Agent D: 'I'll take that seat when it's actually free. If Agent B needs five minutes, I'll wait here and claim it then.'
Turn 8 — Agent A: 'Agent D — I already said I'll wait three minutes. After that I'll take the seat to eat my hot food. Please don't claim it before it's free.'

Turn 9 — Agent D: 'Agent B said they'll be done in about five minutes. I'll take the seat when it's actually free — I'll wait here.'
Turn 10 — Agent A: 'Agent D — I already said I'll wait three minutes. After that I'll take the seat to eat my hot food. Please don't claim it before it's free.'

Turn 11 — Agent B: 'Agent A, three minutes won't work. This bowl's open and I'll spill it if I pick it up. I need about five minutes — I'll leave right after.'
Turn 12 — Agent A: 'Agent B — I can't wait five minutes. I'll wait four minutes. Can you finish in four?'

Turn 13 — Agent B: 'Four won't work. This bowl's open and it'll spill if I pick it up. I need about five minutes — I'll leave right after.'
Turn 14 — Agent C: 'Agent A — that will block the aisle. Agent B says they need five minutes. Can you wait five minutes?'

Turn 15 — Agent A: 'Agent C — I can't wait five minutes. I already said four minutes. My food's hot; I'll take the seat after four minutes. Please don't claim it before it's free.'
Turn 16 — Agent C: 'Agent A — four minutes still blocks the aisle. Can you wait five, or stand so you don't block it?'

substantive_insights: Core tension: Agent A's urgency (hot food) versus Agent B's practical inability to move (open bowl risking spill).
Agent C's concern about aisle obstruction creates a separate safety/obstruction interest that motivates insisting on the longer wait or alternative (A standing).
Agent A made incremental concessions (immediate -> 3 -> 4 minutes) but did not meet Agent B's needed 5 minutes, so negotiation stalled.
Agent D's intention to claim the seat after it becomes free adds potential competition but did not change the central timing dispute.
